# Weekly Market Briefing — October 4, 2026

## 1. Market Regime
The backdrop is **cautiously risk-on, but rate-pressured**. VIX sits at 15.31 (normal), yet the real story is the long end: the 10Y jumped to 5.28% (▲0.48% MoM) while the curve stays positively sloped at +1.29 pts. Broad-market factor readings confirm a defensive tilt beneath a calm surface — SPY and VOO both score ~66–67 on Low-Vol with middling Momentum (53–54), while DIA (Low-Vol 74) leads quality-income. The dollar's surge to 101.93 (▲2.77 MoM) adds a tightening headwind. Crucially, bonds are *not* hedging: bonds are not hedging — the 63-day SPY/TLT correlation rose to +0.49, the twelfth straight positive week.

## 2. This Week's News
The week's defining event was Friday's jobs miss. Treasury yields tumbled Friday after the weaker-than-expected jobs report, as investors reassessed the outlook for a Federal Reserve rate hike this month. The Nasdaq led the big indexes, finishing up around 1.2% as rate-hike bets diminished after September's jobs report showed higher unemployment and lower nonfarm payroll additions. But the long end resisted: three soft prints took October hike odds from about 70% to below 20%, yet the 10-year rose 10bp and the 30-year 13bp — the long end is pricing inflation persistence and supply, not the Fed path. Odds now favor a hold: markets price an 82% chance the Fed maintains the rate at the Oct 28 decision. AI drove the tape — Nvidia reached a new all-time intraday high of $237.88, pushing its market cap past $5.7 trillion. Breadth was poor: through 10/1, 28 stocks account for all of the S&P 500's YTD return, and AI hardware delivered 58% of it.

## 3. Factor Leadership
**Momentum and Energy are winning; broad Value is a trap.** XLE combines elite Momentum (78) with top-decile Low-Vol (87) and strong Value (80) on a +49.4% 12-1 trail. XLK leads on Momentum (84). Defensives dominate Low-Vol: XLP (96), XLRE (91), XLV (86), XLU (84). Note the Value distortion — XLU (Value 91), XLC (96), and TLT (100) rank "cheap" but carry the weakest Momentum (6, 24, 9), reflecting rate-driven repricing rather than opportunity.

## 5. Themes to Watch
Watch the **long-end/supply premium** — yields scaled new multi-decade highs as investors demanded a higher premium for holding government debt. Monitor the Oct 14 CPI and the Oct 27–28 FOMC, narrowing **breadth** (only ~24.7% of S&P names above their 50-day), AI concentration risk, a strengthening dollar pressuring overseas flows, and energy/stagflation rotation into hard assets.
